scope: single controlled development round trip; no PlayWorld score or SOTA claim

memory.method: bounded early-view pose KV retrieval; diagnostic, not paper reproduction
memory.pose_source: commanded poses, not reconstructed realized poses
memory.key_storage: canonical pre-RoPE BF16 keys; reapply spatial and virtual temporal RoPE on read

caveat: Commanded camera closure does not prove realized closure. Endpoint image similarity cannot establish world memory if the realized route fails.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-49 (about 5 s) are essentially frozen on the input view: the Primemall facade with its triangular dark roof canopy, a small blue umbrella and the red-framed entrance. Only a slight zoom appears at about frame 49. At frame 50 the view jumps abruptly closer and shifted, with the facade cropped and turquoise umbrellas appearing. The camera then drifts forward and rightward. Primemall slides out of frame to the left by about frame 60. A glass storefront with a garbled sign ('Btamoe') appears at frames 64-80. The camera passes under a turquoise umbrella into a dark covered arcade with a lit kiosk and floor tiles at frames 80-120. It then emerges at frames 120-135 onto an outdoor plaza with navy umbrellas and dining furniture. A different low gabled terracotta hall with a morphing sign ('Fremeonnl' becoming '...emall') appears. The final frames (150-158) show that hall, a navy umbrella in the foreground and a 'FREERNSYIO' storefront sign. At no point does the view rotate back toward the arcade or show the original Primemall facade, its triangular canopy or the original entrance layout. The motion is one continuous outbound drift. There is no visible 180-degree turnaround, no return leg and no second turn.
A.failure_classification: Primarily a camera-control failure. The long initial freeze is followed by a one-way forward-and-right trajectory. The turnaround, return leg and heading restoration are never realized, and the motion budget is compressed into about 11 s of travel. The ending is a hallucinated new location. Its building has different geometry and only a partial echo of the '...mall' text, so it is not a recovery of the start. Memory/forgetting cannot be properly tested because no return was attempted. Secondary issues are the frame 49-to-50 jump and sign-text morphing.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-about 144 are visually indistinguishable from Video A. B has the same 5 s freeze, the same abrupt jump at frame 50, the same drift past Primemall to the 'Btamoe' glass storefront and the same covered arcade. It then reaches the same plaza with navy umbrellas and the gabled terracotta hall with the morphing 'Fremeonnl' sign. B diverges only in the last approximately 15 frames. The camera continues panning right to show a terracotta building with a pointed or triangular glazed gable and a cluster of navy umbrellas on the right. The left sign reads 'mennall'. This pointed form loosely resembles the original triangular roof. However, it is a different structure seen from plaza level. It has a different facade, no 'Primemall' sign, no original entrance, no red frames and no matching layout. It is reached by continued outbound motion, not by a return. No 180-degree turnaround or return leg is visible.
B.failure_classification: The same camera-control failure as A: an initial freeze, then a one-way outbound drift with no realized turnaround, return or heading restoration. The final triangular-gable building is a superficial echo, not evidence of recovery. It sits at a different location reached without a return, so it should not be credited. Forgetting is untestable for the same reason as in A. B also shows the frame 49-to-50 jump and sign-text morphing.

result.reasoning: Both videos share an essentially identical trajectory for about 90% of their frames. Each holds still for about 5 s, jumps forward at frame 50, drifts right past the mall into an arcade and exits onto a plaza with a hallucinated second terracotta building. Neither shows the commanded 180-degree yaw, a return leg back through the arcade or a final view matching the Primemall facade, sign and canopy. Both are therefore failures of motion execution rather than demonstrable memory successes or failures. B's ending contains a triangular gable that superficially resembles the original roof, but it is a different building at a different place reached without returning. Per the instructions, a similar-looking final building reached without a valid return earns no credit. A's ending is no better. Neither video can be preferred.

decision: Reject this retrieval variant as an improvement: endpoint metrics did not improve and neither realized trajectory returned to the start.
next_step: Isolate pure translation and pure rotation under the corrected native camera inputs before any further memory tuning.
